request.deadline: Contract year covering 52 weeks, with architecture assessment by Q3 2027
deliverables: Protocol maintenance including node upgrades, hard fork readiness, and compatible releases at least 2 weeks before every mainnet hard fork
Ecosystem expansion including Keystone and Flex hardware wallet support, CIP-30 dApp connector, and Japanese localisation
User support for Daedalus users, including Japanese-language support
Security and dependency maintenance for Electron, Node.js, wallet-adjacent dependencies, reproducible Nix builds, and signed releases
Architecture assessment covering current state, options, resource estimates, and recommendation
request.recipient: Se7en Labs, Inc. via Intersect administration and milestone-based disbursement controls
request.what: Daedalus Wallet Maintenance and Improvements 2026-2027 delivered by Se7en Labs, Inc.

claims.claim: Daedalus is Cardano's only full-node desktop wallet, running an embedded Cardano node and deriving wallet and governance data directly from chain without third-party APIs or trusted backends.
Daedalus has approximately 4,000 monthly active users according to opt-in telemetry, while the true count is asserted to be meaningfully higher.
Se7en Labs has maintained Daedalus under an IOG contract since January 2026, with that contract closing August 31, 2026.

The team states it shipped Mithril Snapshot Bootstrap, UTxO-HD/LSM backend integration, Apple Silicon builds, the drt release CLI, Nix modernization, and Daedalus 8.0 and 11.0 during the IOG contract period.
The proposal commits to keeping Daedalus compatible with upcoming hard forks by publishing stable compatible releases at least 2 weeks before mainnet activation.
The proposal includes independently verifiable success metrics for release timing and version currency using public GitHub repositories and the Cardano mainnet chain.
All funded outputs are described as public assets under the Apache 2.0 license, including source code, build tooling, documentation, and release artifacts.

The requested withdrawal is 1,785,333 ADA, allocated to 1,666,667 ADA for labor, 33,333 ADA for test hardware, 33,333 ADA for financial audit, and 52,000 ADA for the Intersect budget administration fee.
The proposal states that unspent labor, hardware, and audit funds will be returned to the treasury at contract close.
Intersect is described as administrator and independent milestone verifier, with funds disbursed monthly against verified work and held in a dedicated account before disbursement to Se7en Labs.

summary: The document requests 1,785,333 ADA for a 2026-2027 time-and-materials engagement to maintain and improve Daedalus, centered on protocol compatibility, security maintenance, hardware wallet support, CIP-30, Japanese localisation, user support, signed releases, and an architecture assessment, with Intersect administration and milestone-based disbursement.
